sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Importing the kind names
sections.what: Brings in the list of allowed kind names from the opportunity map data file. Nothing runs here, it only lets the colour lookup be checked against real kind names.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the colour lookup in step with the kinds the data actually uses.
sections.watch_out: If kind names change in the data file, the colour lookup here must change too, or the type checker will report it.

sections.name: chip
sections.title: Filter chip look
sections.what: Returns the style text for a filter chip. A selected chip is filled dark with white text, and an unselected chip is white with a border that turns red on hover.
sections.why: Likely reason: filter buttons should look the same everywhere on the map.
sections.watch_out: The class text must stay written out in full, because the styling tool only includes class names it can find as complete text.

sections.name: KIND_TONE
sections.title: Colour style for each kind
sections.what: Gives each kind its own look: problems are red-tinted, opportunities are gold, and whitespace is a white box with a dashed border.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user tell the three kinds apart at a glance, with the dashed style suggesting an empty gap.
sections.watch_out: The lookup must have an entry for every kind, so adding a new kind requires adding a new line here.

summary: Holds two small style helpers for the opportunity map: the look of filter buttons and the colour style for each kind of opportunity.
purpose: Keeps the look of filter chips and the kind colours in one place so the opportunity map looks consistent wherever they appear.
why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the names. Likely reason: the styling is shared by several components so it is defined once.
how: 1. Imports the list of kind names from the opportunity map data file. 2. Provides a function that returns the style text for a chip, filled dark when selected and outlined when not. 3. Provides a lookup that gives each kind its colour style.
inputs: A true or false value for whether a chip is selected, and a kind name for the colour lookup.
outputs: Style text strings that components use as class names.
risks: Class names are written out in full so the styling tool can find them. Building them from parts would silently drop the styles. A new kind added to the data file must also be added to the lookup, or the type checker will report it.
debug: If a chip looks unstyled, check that its class text was not built from parts. If a kind has no colour, check that it appears in the lookup and in the kind list of the data file.
